newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Indonesia expects continued good U.S. relations.
newsitem.headline: Indonesia expects continued good U.S. relations.

text.p: Indonesia expected good bilateral relations with the United States to continue following the re-election of President Bill Clinton, a senior Foreign Ministry official said on Wednesday.
"I believe American policy towards Indonesia will not change," Nazaruddin Nasution, director for American affairs at the ministry, told Reuters.
"We know...the United States would like to strengthen bilateral ties in the fields of investment, trade and economic matters," he added.
He said Washington "would like to know more about Indonesia in terms of human rights, democracy".
But he described the personal relationship between Clinton and Indonesia's President Suharto as "very good", noting they had met three times over the past three years.
Official sources said they did not expect the foreign funding row involving the Democratic Party during the election campaign to harm relations.
During the campaign, Republicans raised the question of donations to the Democrats by people connected with Indonesia's Lippo Group headed by the wealthy Riady family.
The official sources noted that Foreign Minister Ali Alatas had said the donations had nothing to do with the Indonesian government.

One source said the future of the issue depended on how it was handled in Congress, but added: "The Indonesian government would like to see no effect whatsoever from this campaign on Indonesian state relations."
